title: The price of the floor
question: Why not a safe ladder and the rest in stocks? Does our floor bought in 2028 beat the rival that keeps the 2028 deposit in stocks and locks the bottom in 2031, on our own model paths, and what does it give up?
serves: North stars 3 and 4; Investment Strategy (the IPS's 'balance growth, risk, liquidity, funding reliability, and financial flexibility') and Portfolio Analysis
essence: We built the plan two mock judges preferred (bonds for the cheques, the rest in stocks until 2031) and ran it beside ours on the same 200,000 model futures.

Its cheques are just as safe and its gift is about $15,000 bigger on average, but the bottom Laura could promise co-sponsors drops under $100,000 about one time in fifteen to twenty (ours about one in a hundred), nearly always after a stock crash; the extra is simply pay for carrying that crash, and it disappears if stocks earn under about 3% a year.
So the IPS should answer that plan by name of idea, not by rival, in one paragraph that states the price out loud.
decided: 3-0 ADOPT: one paragraph answering 'why not a safe ladder and the rest in stocks?' with the unsliced numbers and the price, replacing V39 para 7's 60/40 sentences (and one more cut the rewrite thread picks)
3-0: 'same price, different risk' dropped as a phrase (it isn't the same price; we pay the stock premium and say so)
3-0: the worst-5% slice, the premium test and the 3% break-even stay out of the IPS; they are the Final Report's table and our answer if a judge asks
Kai lost his round-1 bet: 93-94% of the rival's sub-$100k bottoms follow a 2028-30 stock loss
seeds: Is the bottom Laura can quote worth more than its dollar size, because a lead gift draws others (bank #6)? Price the co-sponsor effect of a $95k v $140k bottom in a crash year
Which 19 words pay for the paragraph: the 97-in-100 top line, the one-in-thirty line, or something else?
